trees.title: Linnean Classification of Medically Important Bacteria (Table 5-1)
trees.summary: Master taxonomic scheme classifying bacteria by cell wall architecture (rigid, flexible, absent), free-living capacity, Gram stain, morphology, and oxygen requirements.

root.step: Nature of the Bacterial Cell Wall
root.prompt: Evaluate cell wall architecture: rigid peptidoglycan wall, flexible thin wall, or absent wall [L1 p57]

next.step: Growth Capability: Free-Living vs. Obligate Intracellular
next.prompt: Can the organism grow on artificial laboratory media without living host cells? [L1 p57]
Evaluate crystal violet retention: thick peptidoglycan vs outer membrane LPS [L1 p15, 57]
Determine morphology (cocci vs bacilli) and sporulation capacity [L1 p8, 58]

branches.label: Spherical cells (Cocci in clusters or chains)

outcome.name: Gram-Positive Cocci: Staphylococcus & Streptococcus
outcome.clues: Staphylococcus (grape-like clusters; S. aureus, S. epidermidis) and Streptococcus (chains or pairs; S. pneumoniae, S. pyogenes) [L1 p8, 58].

outcome.name: Spore-Forming Gram-Positive Rods: Bacillus & Clostridium
outcome.clues: Bacillus (aerobic spore-former; B. anthracis) and Clostridium (anaerobic spore-former; C. tetani, C. botulinum) [L1 p52, 58].

outcome.name: Non-Spore-Forming Gram-Positive Rods: Corynebacterium & Listeria
outcome.clues: Non-spore-forming Gram-positive bacilli include Corynebacterium (diphtheroids) and Listeria [L1 p58].

branches.label: Gram-Negative (Outer membrane, LPS endotoxin, periplasmic space)

next.prompt: Determine morphology (cocci, straight rods, curved rods) and primary niche [L1 p56, 59, 60]

outcome.name: Gram-Negative Cocci: Neisseria Genus
outcome.clues: Kidney bean-shaped diplococci: Neisseria meningitidis (meningococcus) and Neisseria gonorrhoeae (gonococcus) [L1 p8, 59].

outcome.name: Gram-Negative Straight Bacilli: Enteric, Respiratory & Zoonotic
outcome.clues: Enteric: E. coli, Salmonella, Shigella, Klebsiella, Proteus, Pseudomonas; Respiratory: Haemophilus, Bordetella, Legionella; Zoonotic: Brucella, Francisella, Yersinia [L1 p56, 59].

outcome.name: Gram-Negative Curved Rods: Vibrio, Campylobacter & Helicobacter
outcome.clues: Comma-shaped Vibrio cholerae, microaerophilic Campylobacter jejuni, and Helicobacter pylori [L1 p8, 60].

outcome.name: Acid-Fast Bacilli: Mycobacterium Genus
outcome.clues: High lipid/mycolic acid content resists standard Gram stain; retains carbolfuchsin red on Ziehl-Neelsen stain (M. tuberculosis) [L1 p33, 60].

outcome.name: Obligate Intracellular Bacteria: Rickettsia & Chlamydia
outcome.clues: Cannot replicate on artificial cell-free media; rely strictly on host cell ATP and intracellular cytoplasm [L1 p57, 60, 63].

outcome.name: Spirochetes: Treponema, Borrelia & Leptospira
outcome.clues: Spiral, flexible, slender undulating rods; require darkfield or fluorescent microscopy (Treponema pallidum, Borrelia, Leptospira) [L1 p8, 57, 60].

outcome.name: Wall-Less Bacteria: Mycoplasma Genus
outcome.clues: Completely lacks peptidoglycan cell wall; bounded only by a triple-layered cell membrane containing sterols; pleomorphic (Mycoplasma pneumoniae) [L1 p32, 57, 60].

trees.title: Bacterial Classification by Oxygen Response & Enzymes (Table 6.1)
trees.summary: Diagnostic pathway classifying bacteria by atmospheric oxygen requirement, metabolic tolerance, and presence of detoxifying enzymes (Superoxide Dismutase & Catalase).

root.prompt: Evaluate bacterial growth in the presence vs. absence of atmospheric oxygen [L3 p14, 15]

outcome.name: Obligate Aerobe (SOD + Catalase Present)
outcome.clues: Requires atmospheric oxygen for energy production via cellular respiration; possesses both superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase to detoxify O2- and H2O2 (e.g., Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa) [L3 p14, 15, 16].

branches.label: Grows With or Without Oxygen (Respiration or Fermentation)

outcome.name: Facultative Anaerobe (SOD + Catalase Present)
outcome.clues: Utilizes oxygen for respiration when present, but switches to anaerobic fermentation in its absence; possesses both superoxide dismutase and catalase (e.g., Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus) [L3 p14, 15, 16].

branches.label: Killed by Atmospheric Oxygen (Lacks Detoxifying Enzymes)

outcome.name: Obligate Anaerobe (SOD & Catalase Absent)
outcome.clues: Incapable of aerobic respiration; killed by toxic oxygen radicals because it completely lacks both superoxide dismutase and catalase (e.g., Clostridium tetani, Clostridium botulinum) [L3 p14, 15, 16].

outcome.name: Microaerophile (Grows at Low O2 Concentrations)
outcome.clues: Grows best in low oxygen tensions; damaged by atmospheric 20% oxygen levels; possesses superoxide dismutase and catalase (e.g., Campylobacter jejuni, Helicobacter pylori) [L3 p15, 16].

outcome.name: Aerotolerant Anaerobe (SOD Present, Catalase Absent)
outcome.clues: Exclusively fermentative metabolism; tolerates oxygen presence because it possesses superoxide dismutase, but lacks catalase [L3 p15, 16].

trees.title: Classification by Nutritional Requirement Flowchart (Slide 32)
trees.summary: Step-by-step metabolic flowchart from Lecture 3 Slide 32 classifying organisms by primary carbon source (CO2 autotroph vs organic heterotroph) and energy source (photo- vs chemo-).

root.prompt: Evaluate whether the organism uses inorganic CO2 or organic compounds as its principal carbon source [L3 p32]

branches.label: Autotrophs (Use Inorganic CO2 as Sole Carbon Source)

next.prompt: Determine the source of energy: sunlight vs inorganic chemical oxidation [L3 p32, 33]

outcome.name: Photoautotrophs
outcome.clues: Use light energy to fix inorganic CO2 into organic carbon (e.g., photosynthetic cyanobacteria) [L3 p32, 33].

outcome.name: Chemoautotrophs (Chemolithotrophs)
outcome.clues: Oxidize inorganic chemical compounds (iron, sulfur, nitrifying bacteria) to obtain energy while using CO2 as carbon source [L3 p32, 33].

branches.label: Heterotrophs (Require Organic Compounds as Carbon Source)
branches.organismGroup: Organotrophs requiring preformed organic nutrients [L3 p32, 34]

next.prompt: Determine the source of energy: sunlight vs organic chemical oxidation [L3 p32, 34]

outcome.name: Photoheterotrophs
outcome.clues: Use sunlight for energy but require organic compounds as their source of carbon (e.g., purple non-sulfur bacteria) [L3 p32, 34].

outcome.name: Chemoheterotrophs (Medical Bacteria & Human Pathogens)
outcome.clues: Derive both carbon and energy from organic compounds (glucose, amino acids); includes all medically important bacteria, normal flora, and parasites feeding on living organic host matter [L3 p32, 34, 35].
